chapter: Countess Johnson's band and the Kansas City scene
title: Why Basie got publicity and Andy Kirk did not
summary: Basie had Benny Goodman and John Hammond behind him, while Kirk lacked backers though he was most popular in Kansas City.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You know. For an example, when Andy Kirk was winnin' all the battles, when Basie came in and won such acclaim. But he had the right publicity and everything behind him, Basie, you know.
But Andy Kirk, he didn't have the right people that really cared enough to give him a build-up, you know.
Basie ended up with Benny Goodman and John Hammond behind him--
Well, that's the point, isn't it?
Yeah, and that put them right on top. But Andy Kirk was the most popular band in Kansas City as far as the--
I mean, the thing is, that at the same time, it doesn't seem to me, it was a rather pretty band when Mary was playing with it, but it didn't really have the drive of Basie's, did it?
